b. Click on three dots (...) present on right side of the your newly created teams channel and Get link to the channel.
c. copy the text from the link between /channel and /, decode it using online url decoder and copy it to use as channelId.
d. copy the text of groupId parameter from link to use as groupId.

metadata.title: Rubrik DSPM Violation Remediation
metadata.description: Incident-triggered playbook that remediates Rubrik Security Cloud (RSC) DSPM violations. Branches on eventType: for SecurityViolation it retrieves the violation, exports the violation-files CSV and the remediation-actions log (create -> poll Download Bar -> download bytes -> upload to a blob container -> generate SAS link), lists the violation file hits, quarantines each file via the RubrikQuarantineFiles sub-playbook, notifies the file owner in Teams, and marks the violation REMEDIATED only when every quarantine succeeded. For ClassificationResultsAvailable (no DSPM license) it runs a reduced flow: list file hits (objectId + snapshotId) -> quarantine -> notify. Both flows write a final comment to the Microsoft Sentinel incident.

metadata.title: Rubrik Quarantine Files
metadata.description: This playbook is an HTTP Request-triggered child playbook that quarantines a batch of files reported by a Rubrik Security Cloud DSPM violation. It is called by the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook with the whole files array in a single call and iterates internally, so it runs once per incident instead of once per file. It branches on objectType into three paths: ONEDRIVE files are quarantined via Microsoft Graph (the analyst is asked once per run for a share link to a single destination quarantine folder via a Teams Adaptive Card; that link is resolved once up front with GET /v1.0/shares/{link}/driveItem into a destination driveId and item id, so the destination is decoupled from each file's source drive and no per-file folder lookup or create is performed. Each file is then resolved directly by drive and path - the drive from the RSC snappable identity, driveOwnerUpn for OneDrive or siteUrl for SharePoint, and the path from filePath/nativePath - downloaded, uploaded into the single destination folder with @microsoft.graph.conflictBehavior=rename so same-named files from different drives do not overwrite each other, and the source deleted only after a confirmed upload; if the file cannot be resolved at that exact path the file is reported Failed and is never matched by a tenant-wide search); NTFS (Windows Fileset) files are quarantined via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (the device is resolved by physicalHost, each file's SHA1 is resolved via advanced hunting scoped by DeviceId, FileName and FolderPath, and a StopAndQuarantineFile machine action is created and polled for up to 20 minutes). Note that RSC supplies physicalHost only on SecurityViolation events, so Windows Fileset files arriving from a Classification event are reported Failed with an explanatory message rather than silently skipped; any other objectType returns NotImplemented. A single app registration (client id/secret in Key Vault) authenticates both Microsoft Graph and MDE; only the OAuth2 token scope differs per branch. The playbook returns { status, results: [ { filename, status, newLocation, error } ] } to the caller.
prerequisites: 1. A single Azure AD app registration is used for BOTH Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Grant it (all admin-consented):
a. Microsoft Graph APPLICATION permissions: Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All, User.Read.All.
b. WindowsDefenderATP (Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) APPLICATION permissions: Machine.ReadWrite.All (or Machine.StopAndQuarantine) and AdvancedQuery.Read.All.
2. Store the app registration credentials in Key Vault and obtain the Key Vault name and tenantId.
a. Create a Key Vault with a unique name.

b. Go to KeyVault -> secrets, click Generate/import and create TWO secrets using EXACTLY these names (they are fixed in the playbook and are not deployment parameters): 'Graph-App-ClientId' holding the app registration's Application (client) ID, and 'Graph-App-ClientSecret' holding its client secret VALUE. The same credentials authenticate both Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
NOTE: Make sure the Permission model in the Access Configuration of the Key Vault is set to 'Vault access policy'. If not, change it to 'Vault access policy'.
3. For the ONEDRIVE branch, a Microsoft Teams team and channel are required for the Adaptive Card that collects the quarantine folder share link.

3a. Create the destination quarantine folder in OneDrive or SharePoint before running the playbook and have its share link ready (Share -> Copy link). All files in a run are moved into that single folder regardless of which drive they came from, and same-named files are renamed rather than overwritten. The app registration must be able to read the link, so prefer a link scoped to people in your organization over a link restricted to named individuals. Exclude this quarantine folder from DSPM scan scope, otherwise the quarantined copies are scanned again and raise fresh violations for files that were just remediated.

4. For the NTFS branch, the target file shares must be hosted on devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and resolvable by their physicalHost / computerDnsName. RSC supplies physicalHost only on SecurityViolation events; Windows Fileset files arriving from a Classification event cannot be quarantined and are reported Failed with an explanatory message. KNOWN LIMITATION: the file's SHA1 is resolved from the most recent DeviceFileEvents record (Defender retains roughly 30 days) and StopAndQuarantineFile is keyed by that hash. If the file has since been modified or deleted, Defender reports the action as successful even though nothing was quarantined.

5. This playbook is a prerequisite for the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook and must be deployed first, in the same resource group. RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation calls this playbook as a sub-playbook (via its RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName parameter) once per incident to quarantine the violation files.

1. Go to your logic app -> API connections -> Select the Teams connection resource.
2. Go to General -> edit API connection.
6. The Key Vault connection uses the managed identity and does not require an interactive sign-in.

instructionSteps.description: Use the following step-by-step instructions to deploy the Rubrik Microsoft Sentinel data connector manually with Azure Functions (Deployment via Visual Studio Code).
instructionSteps.title: Option 2 - Manual Deployment of Azure Functions

instructionSteps.description:
**1. Deploy a Function App**

> **NOTE:** You will need to [prepare VS code](https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-first-function-python#prerequisites) for Azure function development.

1. Download the [Azure Function App](https://aka.ms/sentinel-RubrikDataConnector-functionapp) file. Extract archive to your local development computer.
2. Start VS Code. Choose File in the main menu and select Open Folder.
3. Select the top level folder from extracted files.
4. Choose the Azure icon in the Activity bar, then in the **Azure: Functions** area, choose the **Deploy to function app** button.
If you aren't already signed in, choose the Azure icon in the Activity bar, then in the **Azure: Functions** area, choose **Sign in to Azure**
If you're already signed in, go to the next step.
5. Provide the following information at the prompts:

	a. **Select folder:** Choose a folder from your workspace or browse to one that contains your function app.

	b. **Select Subscription:** Choose the subscription to use.

	c. Select **Create new Function App in Azure** (Don't choose the Advanced option)

	d. **Enter a globally unique name for the function app:** Type a name that is valid in a URL path. The name you type is validated to make sure that it's unique in Azure Functions. (e.g. RubrikXXXXX).

	e. **Select a runtime:** Choose Python 3.12.

	f. Select a location for new resources. For better performance and lower costs choose the same [region](https://azure.microsoft.com/regions/) where Microsoft Sentinel is located.

6. Deployment will begin. A notification is displayed after your function app is created and the deployment package is applied.
7. Go to Azure Portal for the Function App configuration.

**2. Configure the Function App**

1. In the Function App, select the Function App Name and select **Configuration**.
2. In the **Application settings** tab, select **+ New application setting**.
3. Add each of the following application settings individually, with their respective values (case-sensitive):
		WorkspaceResourceId
		Location
		AnomaliesTableName
		RansomwareAnalysisTableName
		ThreatHuntsTableName
		EventsTableName
		ViolationTableName
		AZURE_DATA_COLLECTION_ENDPOINT
		DCR_WEBHOOK_RULE_ID
		DCR_EVENTS_RULE_ID
		SCOPE
		RubrikInstanceUrl
		RubrikClientId
		RubrikClientSecret
		LogLevel
 - For Azure Government, set SCOPE to https://monitor.azure.us/.default and use the Gov Data Collection Endpoint.
 - This connector authenticates using the Function App's System-Assigned Managed Identity, which is granted the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role on the Data Collection Rules by the ARM template.
 - RubrikInstanceUrl / RubrikClientId / RubrikClientSecret are the Rubrik Security Cloud service-account credentials used only by the Violation classification hit-count gate.
4. Once all application settings have been entered, click **Save**.
**Post Deployment steps**

1. Go to Azure function Overview page and Click on **"Functions"** tab.
2. Click on the function called **"RubrikHttpStarter"**.
3. Go to **"GetFunctionurl"** and copy the function url.

instructionSteps.description:
Follow the Rubrik User Guide instructions to [Add a Webhook](https://docs.rubrik.com/en-us/saas/saas/common/adding_webhook.html) to begin receiving event information  
 1. Select the Microsoft Sentinel as the webhook Provider 
 2. Enter the desired Webhook name 
 3. Enter the URL part from copied Function-url as the webhook URL endpoint and replace **{functionname}**  with **"RubrikAnomalyOrchestrator"**, for the Rubrik Microsoft Sentinel Solution 
 4. Select the EventType as Anomaly 
 5. Select the following severity levels: Critical, Warning, Informational 
 6. Choose multiple log types, if desired, when running **"RubrikEventsOrchestrator"** 
 7. Repeat the same steps to add webhooks for Anomaly Detection Analysis, Threat Hunt, Other Events and Violation.
   

 NOTE: while adding webhooks for Anomaly Detection Analysis, Threat Hunt, Other Events and Violation, replace **{functionname}**  with **"RubrikRansomwareOrchestrator"**, **"RubrikThreatHuntOrchestrator"**, **"RubrikEventsOrchestrator"** and **"RubrikViolationOrchestrator"** respectively in copied function-url.

 NOTE: For Violation (classification) events, **"RubrikViolationOrchestrator"** applies a hit-count gate: classification-results events are ingested only when Rubrik Security Cloud reports policy hits > 0. This gate uses the **RubrikInstanceUrl**, **RubrikClientId**, and **RubrikClientSecret** application settings configured in Step 2.

instructionSteps.title: 3. Create the webhooks in Rubrik Security Cloud
instructionSteps.description: Create one webhook per event category. Each webhook posts to the same Data Collection Endpoint but targets a different stream, which determines the destination table.

parameters.content:
#### Webhook authentication
In Rubrik Security Cloud, create each webhook with the **Microsoft Sentinel** provider and set the authentication type to **OAuth 2.0** using these values:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Grant type | `client_credentials` |
| Token URL | `<Microsoft Entra ID Token Endpoint>/<Tenant ID>/oauth2/v2.0/token` |
| Client ID | `<Application ID>` |
| Client secret | `<Application Secret>` |
| Scope | `https://monitor.azure.com//.default` |

Replace `<Microsoft Entra ID Token Endpoint>` with the Microsoft Entra ID authentication endpoint for your Azure cloud, and `<Tenant ID>`, `<Application ID>` and `<Application Secret>` with the values for the app registration created above.

#### Webhook URLs
Use the following URL for each webhook, replacing `<Data Collection Endpoint Uri>` and `<Data Collection Rule Immutable ID>` with the values copied above, and `<Stream Name>` with the stream for that event category:

`<Data Collection Endpoint Uri>/dataCollectionRules/<Data Collection Rule Immutable ID>/streams/<Stream Name>?api-version=2023-01-01`

| Event category | Stream name | Destination table |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anomaly | `Custom-Rubrik_Anomaly_Data` | `Rubrik_Anomaly_Data_CL` |
| Ransomware analysis | `Custom-Rubrik_Ransomware_Data` | `Rubrik_Ransomware_Data_CL` |
| Threat hunt | `Custom-Rubrik_ThreatHunt_Data` | `Rubrik_ThreatHunt_Data_CL` |
| All other events | `Custom-Rubrik_Events_Data` | `Rubrik_Events_Data_CL` |

Scope each webhook's event-type and severity filters to the matching category so that events are routed to the correct table.

connectorUiConfig.title: Rubrik Security Cloud Security Events (Push)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The Rubrik Security Cloud Security Events (Push) connector ingests security events from Rubrik Security Cloud into Microsoft Sentinel in real time using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) Push pattern. Rubrik Security Cloud webhooks authenticate with OAuth 2.0 and post events directly to the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API, with no intermediate compute to deploy or operate. Events are routed to per-category tables for anomalies, ransomware analysis, threat hunts, and all other events.

instructionSteps.description: This connector lets Rubrik Security Cloud push security events directly to Microsoft Sentinel through the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API.

parameters.content:
#### Automated configuration
Selecting **Deploy** creates the Log Analytics tables and a Data Collection Rule (DCR), registers a Microsoft Entra application, links the DCR to that application, and assigns the required role. Rubrik Security Cloud then uses the resulting credentials to send events securely to the DCR.

instructionSteps.title: 3. Create the webhooks in Rubrik Security Cloud
instructionSteps.description: Create one webhook per event category. Each webhook posts to the same Data Collection Endpoint but targets a different stream, which determines the destination table.

parameters.content:
#### Webhook authentication
In Rubrik Security Cloud, create each webhook with the **Microsoft Sentinel** provider and set the authentication type to **OAuth 2.0** using these values:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Grant type | `client_credentials` |
| Token URL | `<Microsoft Entra ID Token Endpoint>/<Tenant ID>/oauth2/v2.0/token` |
| Client ID | `<Application ID>` |
| Client secret | `<Application Secret>` |
| Scope | `https://monitor.azure.com//.default` |

Replace `<Microsoft Entra ID Token Endpoint>` with the Microsoft Entra ID authentication endpoint for your Azure cloud, and `<Tenant ID>`, `<Application ID>` and `<Application Secret>` with the values for the app registration created above.

#### Webhook URLs
Use the following URL for each webhook, replacing `<Data Collection Endpoint Uri>` and `<Data Collection Rule Immutable ID>` with the values copied above, and `<Stream Name>` with the stream for that event category:

`<Data Collection Endpoint Uri>/dataCollectionRules/<Data Collection Rule Immutable ID>/streams/<Stream Name>?api-version=2023-01-01`

| Event category | Stream name | Destination table |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anomaly | `Custom-Rubrik_Anomaly_Data` | `Rubrik_Anomaly_Data_CL` |
| Ransomware analysis | `Custom-Rubrik_Ransomware_Data` | `Rubrik_Ransomware_Data_CL` |
| Threat hunt | `Custom-Rubrik_ThreatHunt_Data` | `Rubrik_ThreatHunt_Data_CL` |
| All other events | `Custom-Rubrik_Events_Data` | `Rubrik_Events_Data_CL` |

Scope each webhook's event-type and severity filters to the matching category so that events are routed to the correct table.
